name: Oubliette
oracle_text: When this enchantment enters, target creature phases out until this enchantment leaves the battlefield. Tap that creature as it phases in this way. (Auras and Equipment phase out with it. While permanents are phased out, they're treated as though they don't exist.)
blocked_sentences: When this enchantment enters, target creature phases out until this enchantment leaves the battlefield.
Tap that creature as it phases in this way.

needs.what: an `until_leaves` (or `link`) option on the `phase_out` op that suspends the untap-step phase-in for as long as the source permanent is on the battlefield, plus the linked selector that reads those permanents back -- the phasing twin of exile's O-Ring link, so a `leaves_battlefield` trigger on the same card can name what its own `phase_out` sent away and phase it back in
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `phase_out` in src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_board.py takes only `objects` and calls `turn.phase_out`, which sets `obj.phased_out` with no record of what caused it; the untap walk in src/automtg/engine/turn.py (`going_in`) then phases the permanent back in at its controller's very next untap step unconditionally. That is a fixed one-turn duration, not "until this enchantment leaves the battlefield" -- the creature would come back with Oubliette still on the battlefield, which is a materially different card. `exile`'s `until_leaves` is the right shape but the wrong zone: exiling instead of phasing loses counters, attachments and continuous effects, and fires zone-change triggers that phasing deliberately does not. `selector_keys` has `exiled_with` for the exile link and nothing equivalent for phasing, and no selector can name a phased-out permanent at all, so even a `leaves_battlefield` trigger on Oubliette cannot find its victim.

needs.what: a way to say "tap that creature as it phases in this way" -- either a `tapped: true` option on the linked phase-in that applies as the permanent returns, or a `phased_in` trigger event exposing the returning permanent so a `tap` can be aimed at it
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `turn.phase_in` restores the permanent untouched and only emits a `phased_in` state event; `phased_in` is not in `trigger_events`, so no ability can see it. The `tap` op exists but has no object to name: nothing links the returning creature to Oubliette, and by the time Oubliette's `leaves_battlefield` trigger would resolve the creature is still phased out and unselectable. Sequencing a plain `tap` at the enters trigger instead would tap it now rather than on the way back, which is a different card.
